title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
official_title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
summary: Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lets the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence jointly authorize the targeting of people reasonably believed to be outside the United States to collect foreign intelligence, for up to a year at a time, and states that the regular FISA court-order process is not required for that targeting. This bill moves the date those authorities shut off from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026 and makes no other change.
brief: Moves the shut-off date for FISA Title VII surveillance authorities from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026, with nothing else attached.

top_lines.headline: What Title VII Authorizes
subs: Attorney General and DNI jointly authorize targeting of people located abroad
Each joint authorization runs up to 1 year
Regular FISA court-order process not required for that targeting
Providers can be directed in writing to supply information and assistance
FBI queries of the collected data using U.S. person terms need supervisor approval

top_lines.headline: What This Bill Changes
subs: Shut-off date moved from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026
Same date change applied to a wiretap-law conforming amendment
No new limits, oversight, or reporting attached

top_lines.headline: Effective Date
subs: Takes effect on the earlier of enactment or June 11, 2026

likelihoodReason: Taken up under suspension of the rules, which requires a two-thirds majority, and rejected 198-218 on June 11, 2026 (Roll no. 221) after forty minutes of debate. The sponsor is a Republican and the bill had no cosponsors. A failed floor vote ends its progress in this Congress.

sections.label: Section 1 — Extension of Authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978

items.main: Amends Section 403(b)(1) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) by striking June 12, 2026 and inserting July 2, 2026.
items.detail: Section 403(b)(1) is the sunset clause: the United States Code prints a Repeal of Section note under the Title VII sections, including 50 U.S.C. 1881 and 1881a, stating that section 403(b)(1) repeals them effective on the date it names. The bill text records that date as most recently set by Public Law 119-87. The bill changes only the date; the targeting and minimization procedures, the query restrictions on the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the certification and court-review process are left as they stand.

items.main: Applies the same date change to Section 403(b)(2), which governs a conforming amendment to the federal criminal wiretap statute.
items.detail: Section 403(b)(2) of Public Law 110-261 provides that, on the sunset date, 18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(a)(ii)(A) is amended by striking the words or a court order pursuant to section 704 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. Subparagraph (A) is one of two showings that let a communications provider lawfully furnish surveillance assistance, the other being a written certification under subparagraph (B); the strike removes a FISA section 704 order from the list of qualifying court orders. The bill moves the date that strike takes effect from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026.

items.main: Sets both date changes to take effect on the earlier of the date of enactment or June 11, 2026.
items.detail: June 11, 2026 is the day before the June 12, 2026 shut-off the bill was written to move, so the amendments would attach before that date even if enactment came later.

underreported.summary: Moves the effective date of a conforming amendment to the federal criminal wiretap statute, 18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(a)(ii)(A), from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026. That amendment strikes the reference to a FISA section 704 court order from the list of showings that authorize a communications provider to furnish surveillance assistance.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill is captioned as extending FISA Title VII authorities, and the bill text identifies this paragraph only by its note citation, 18 U.S.C. 2511 note. The provision operates on title 18 of the U.S. Code, not on FISA.

gaps: The bill sets a new July 2, 2026 shut-off date but attaches no condition, review, or reporting requirement to the additional period.
The bill is captioned as extending the Title VII authorities and for other purposes, but the text contains only the two date changes and the effective-date clause.

modified: Section 403(b)(1) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) — Title VII repeal date changed from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026
Section 403(b)(2) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) — effective date of the conforming amendment to 18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(a)(ii)(A) changed from June 12, 2026 to July 2, 2026
